ISSUE No.1:
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself stepped into witness box as PW1.

He deposed that on 05.09.2022 at about 06:15 a.m., when complainant was going to his home at Kalyanpuri f r o m A k s h a r d h a m s i d e a n d r e a c h e d i n f r o n t o f H e r o H o n d a S h o w r o o m , a ____________________________________________________________________ MACP No

No suggestion was given to petitioner by R3/Insurer that offending vehicle was not involved in the accident or was falsely implicated.

11. Further, it is not disputed that respondent No.1/driver Charan Singh was charge-sheeted in the aforesaid criminal case for causing the accident by driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
Thus, prima-facie, it is clear that respondent No.1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner at the time of accident.
12. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the bus.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
14. Respondent Nos.1 & 2, the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, did not lead any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

17. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
18. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.

The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss o f  
e a r n i n g  
c a p a c i t y .

It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities consequent to his injuries.

19. Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to her under the afore-said heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
20.
No medical bill pertaining to the treatment of injuries sustained in accident is relied upon.
Perusal of record shows that petitioner was treated in a Govt. Hospital.
Petitioner has relied on a bill of his Ex.PW1/3 of Singla medical store for a sum of Rs. 206/-.

This bill is dated 02.09.2022 whereas the accident in question took place on 05.09.2022 and hence, it is clear that this Ante dated document has been filed merely with a view to give an impression before the Tribunal that petitioner incurred medical expenses in his treatment, under the belief that the Tribunal shall miss out on such minor detail as the date of the bill.

This speaks volumes about the conduct and character of the ____________________________________________________________________ MACP No. 164/23 JitenderVs. Charan Singh & Ors. Page No. 8 of 18 petitioner.

There is not much to comment upon but at least, the counsel representing the petitioner could have been careful in relying on any such bill prepared prior to the date of accident and unrelated to the accident.
Hence, in view of the above-said discussion, no amount is granted to the petitioner under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
21.
Petitioner has deposed that after the accident, he was taken to LBS Hospital where his MLC was prepared.
MLC of the petitioner shows that he sustained from 'right neck of femur fracture' and the injuries suffered by the petitioner was 'grievous'.

22. In view of this, it is clear the petitioner must have remained under immense pain and suffering for a long time during his treatment and even after his treatment he would not be able to use his limbs properly on account of permanent disability for entire life.

In "Ankur Kapoor Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd, of Supreme Court of India, decided on 06.11.2017, LAWs (SC)-2017-11-51", Hon'ble Apex Court granted additional Rs.3,00,000/ towards pain, agony and trauma in a case where claimant suffered 50% disability in relation to his right arm.

Thereafter as well, on his subsequent visits on 26.12.2022 and 06.02.2023, only partial weight bearing was allowed to him.
He is stated to have underwent operative procedure in the hospital.

Petitioner has not produced any evidence in support of his employment and nature of work.

However, considering the nature and extent of permanent disability suffered by the petitioner, it can reasonably be assumed that petitioner shall face difficulty in his job / work as a supervisor in transport company, as it may involve standing and field work and further even if he takes any other avocation in future, life would not be the same for him as before and his physical capability must have diminished considerably.

In 'New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Sita Ram & Ors.' (MAC App. No. 26/12 decided on 28.03.2014), Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has observed that:-

sentences.text:
Arising out of civil appeal No. 8918 of 2010, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that :-
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning c a p a c i t y  
i n v o l v e s ____________________________________________________________________ MACP No. 164/23 JitenderVs. Charan Singh & Ors. Page No. 12 of 18 three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claim could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether ; (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether inspite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.

For example, if the left hand of the claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or disablement may be around Jitender vs Charan Singh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68100161/
7 60%.
If the claimant was a driver of a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be 100%, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant is clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could performed his clerical functions, in that even the loss of earnings capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter nor 60% which is the actual physical disability but far less.

In fact, there may not be need to award any compensation under the head of 'Loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in Government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities on the consequences of losing his hand....."
In the present case, it would be difficult for the petitioner to do any job involving standing or sitting for long hours.
Thus, total functional disability of petitioner towards whole body is assessed to be 20% for computation of loss of future income.
28. The multiplier of damages has to be determined as per Sarla Verma Vs. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
As per aadhar card and matriculation marksheet, of the petitioner EX. PW1/1, the date of birth of petitioner is 20.09.1990.
Hence, petitioner was 31 years, 11 months and 16 days on the date of accident.
Therefore, multiplier of 16 would be applicable in the present case.
The income of petitioner has already been ascertained hereinabove to be Rs.20,000/- per month.
The annual income of the petitioner comes to Rs.2,40,000/- (i.e. Rs.20,000/- X 12).
Petitioner is also entitled for future compensation @ 40% in view of Pranay Sethi judgment.
Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.

31. Further, admittedly, the petitioner was operated and remained hospitalized.
Thus, it cannot be disputed that the petitioner must have spent reasonable amount for his special diet for the purpose of early recovery post surgery.
Thus, petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards special diet.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant / care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.

In view of above, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded to petitioner as attendant charges.
33. Thus, a total sum of Rs.45,000/-(15,000+15,000+15,000) is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

34. Considering the disability of the petitioner, there remains no doubt that he will not be able to enjoy the basic amenities to the fullest throughout his life.

Though, no specific evidence has been led on this aspect, however, considering the permanent disability of 34% in respect of right lower limb,
this court is of the view that said consequences of the accident would definitely create hindrance in enjoying basic amenities of life.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

LIABILITY 37.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.

As the vehicle was insured with TATA AIG Insurance Company Ltd. on the date of accident,
it is clear that R3/TATA AIG Insurance Company is liable to compensate the petitioner.
Thus, the Respondent No. 3, being insurer of the offending vehicle, is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
INTEREST 38.
The petitioner has conducted the proceedings in this case since year 2022.
Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till date of realization.
